name: The crossroads: MLK Jr. Dr. and Fairburn Rd.
caption: MLK Jr. Drive (State Route 139) in Adamsville. Photo: Thomson200, 2016, CC0, Wikimedia Commons.
note: Old Gordon Road meets Fairburn Road. The Civic Club planned a shopping center here in 1955, the city mapped one in 1970, and the 2020 master plan names it 'Adamsville Village.' There is still no full-service grocery within walking distance.

name: Community Food Center, 3500 MLK Jr. Dr.
caption: Dollar General next to the food center. Photo: John Phelan, 2026, CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.
note: The Atlanta Community Food Bank opened its first in-city Community Food Center here in August 2025, in a former Family Dollar. It serves more than 700 families a month by appointment.

name: Fire Station 9 and City Takers church
caption: Atlanta Fire Station 9. Photo: John Phelan, 2026, CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.
note: In 1955 the Civic Club reported that no fire station stood within 3.5 miles of Fain School. Today Fire Station 9 sits at the crossroads beside a church in a former commercial building.

name: Former Margaret Fain School
caption: Margaret Fain Elementary School, historical photograph (date not recorded). Source: Classmates.com. Used for educational purposes.
note: Built in 1927. The Civic Club called it 'the most important building in the community,' used for meetings, dinners and play. From 2022 it housed Douglass High's ninth-grade campus; APS plans to close it.

name: Old Adamsville Recreation Center
caption: Old Adamsville Recreation Center, 31 Brownlee Rd NW. Image: Google Street View, November 2024 (map controls and a navigation marker removed).
note: Runs senior programs midweek and serves as a warming center. Residents say seniors gather here from Wednesday to Friday.

name: C. T. Martin Natatorium and Recreation Center
caption: C. T. Martin Natatorium and Recreation Center from Harwell Rd NW. Image: Google Street View, February 2025 (map controls cropped out).
note: A 50-meter pool, therapy pool and gym at 3201 MLK Jr. Drive, built on the site of a troubled apartment complex and renamed for Councilmember C. T. Martin in 2017. NPU-H meets here.

name: Cascade Family Skating
caption: Cascade Family Skating, 3335 MLK Jr. Dr. Photo: Family Action. Used for educational purposes.
note: A regional landmark for young people, featured in the 2006 film ATL. Both residents named it as part of Adamsville's identity.

name: Adamsville Regional Health Center
caption: Adamsville Regional Health Center. Photo: Whiting-Turner Contracting Company. Used for educational purposes.
note: Fulton County health center. In 1955 the Civic Club praised 'a fine county health center' but noted that most residents rarely used it.

name: Wilson Mill Park
caption: The 1970 West Adamsville plan, which proposed expanding Wilson Mill Park. Planning Atlanta Collection, GSU Library.
note: Where most community events happen, residents say. In 1955 the Civic Club wrote 'There are no parks in Adamsville'; the 1970 plan proposed growing this park into a community park.

name: Juanita H. Gardner Village
caption: Architectural rendering of Juanita H. Gardner Village released at its groundbreaking. Atlanta Housing. Used for educational purposes.
note: 108 affordable apartments for seniors at 3650 Bakers Ferry Road, opened in December 2024 by Atlanta Housing, Invest Atlanta and the Georgia Department of Community Affairs. Named for a longtime neighborhood leader.

name: Jackson Memorial Baptist Church
caption: Jackson Memorial Baptist Church. Image: Jackson Memorial Baptist Church website. Used for educational purposes.
note: One of the churches at the center of Sunday life. Its pastor, Rev. Dr. Gregory A. Sutton, appears on the 2023 Adamsville Legacy mural.

name: L. P. Miles Elementary
caption: Leonora P. Miles Elementary School. Photo: Homes.com. Used for educational purposes.
note: Began in 1907 as Bethlehem Church School, the first school for African American children in Adamsville-Boulder Park. Renamed in 1967.

name: Benjamin E. Mays High School
caption: Benjamin E. Mays High School. Photo: Homes.com. Used for educational purposes.
note: Residents remember it as one of the most desirable high schools in the city. Its homecoming is one of the neighborhood's yearly events.
